text:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT eu-south1 - control-plane heartbeats missing (2m), API traffic dropped ~97%, GPU pool healthy_nodes=0. Check runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/region-outage

maya: getting 502s from hosted-api in eu-south1, same from SDK tests. Most customers hitting eu-south1 failing.

liam: oncall here, looking at cluster control plane. Can anyone reach apiserver in eu-south1? Trying kubectl get nodes against eu-south1 endpoint.

anya: I can SSH to eu-south1-k8s-03 but kubelet is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, docker daemon is unresponsive. grabbing journal.

noah: cloud-provider status shows network disruption in eu-south1-a and eu-south1-b, BGP withdraws noticed. Provider ticket already opened (CP-8891).

devon: starting failover plan - reroute traffic from eu-south1 to eu-west1 and ams2. Will update routing policy and reduce DNS TTLs.

maya: quick verification - many model-serving pods are OOMKilled or network not reachable. Looks like a network fabric issue, not just control plane.

liam: running emergency command to mark region unhealthy so router will remove it from global pool: `infractl regions set-health eu-south1 unhealthy --reason "control-plane+fabric"`

devon: applying regional fallback policy now: `redwood route update --from eu-south1 --to eu-west1,ams2 --weights 85,15 --ttl 30s`

netops-bot: NOTE: applied temporary BGP workaround to announce more-specifics from peering edge in eu-west1 to speed convergence.

anya: journal snippet from kubelet:
```
Mar 23 10:12:44 kubelet[1234]: watchdog: kernel panic - out of memory
Mar 23 10:12:45 systemd[1]: docker.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Mar 23 10:12:46 kubelet[1234]: kubelet lost connection to apiserver
```

noah: because provider withdrew BGP, nodes couldn't reach our central control plane; cloud's incident says partial region network partition. Not sure when full restoration.

devon: spinning up reserved GPU hosts in eu-west1 and ams2 to absorb model traffic. ETA for GPU readiness ~4-6m for preprovisioned images to finish. liam, can you start canary routing once hosts pass health checks?

liam: will do. launching autoscale override for critical pools: `k8s-autoscaler set --pool gpu-critical --min 6 --max 50 --force`

maya: customers with Reserved Dedicated in eu-south1 - we should notify via status page and support. Opening incident page and status update.

monitoring-bot: INCIDENT-2259 created: INC-2026-2259 - eu-south1 region outage. Zoom bridge: https://zoom.internal/inc-2259. Pager duty escalation sent to infra-oncall.

noah: cost note - shifting traffic to eu-west1 will incur higher spot premiums this hour, and reserved spin-up will increase monthly committed usage if we keep it. We should consider short window failover only, then evaluate need for reserved capacity.

devon: agreed. immediate goal = restore customer-facing SLA. Post-incident we'll evaluate capacity commitments and cross-region redundancy. For now: shift 85% traffic to eu-west1, 15% to ams2 as canary.

liam: canary health checks green for initial model endpoints in eu-west1. Routing change propagated, traffic moving. Monitoring shows request latency up ~30% p95, error rate down from 80% to ~5%.

anya: capturing logs and core dumps for kubelet/kernel OOMs, will attach to incident. Might be provider-side networking + host-level memory pressure.

devon: communications: public status updated, support notified, sales being pinged for high priority customers. postmortem owner: @maya.

maya: on it. I'll own postmortem and runbook gaps. Next steps: monitor for 30m, if stable start controlled reintroduce to eu-south1 once provider confirms BGP/edge stability.

netops-bot: Provider CP ticket updated: maintenance window extended, next update in 20m.

devon: thanks everyone. Keeping channel open. If anything changes, ping #pager. :thumbsup:
